transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ana Soto (StratusHealth - Head of ML), Marcus Li (StratusHealth - Platform), Rachel Kim (StratusHealth - CISO)

Summary (auto): Quick review and signoff of POC acceptance rubric and artifact format. Clarify pass/fail thresholds for latency and quality, agree on workload sizing and reporting artifacts, schedule benchmark run and infra kickoff.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you. we wanted to go through the acceptance rubric today and nail down the go/no-go thresholds and what the deliverables look like. Priya from our side will walk the benchmark plan.
00:22 Ana: Thanks Jordan, yep we're excited. main things for us are latency at p95, cost per 1M tokens, and accuracy on our anonymization checks.
00:35 Marcus: Also we need the infra pattern - we will likely run on our VPC but could do a hosted run for the initial benchmark if that's easier.
01:05 Priya: Quick clarifier - when you say p95 latency what's the target today? And is that for full request (incl. decode) or just model time?
01:30 Ana: We want end-to-end response within 600ms p95 for short prompts (<256 tokens). For longer prompts maybe a different bucket, but p95 600ms is the primary SLA.
01:52 Jordan: Noted. For cost we typically report both tokens and instance-hours; we can provide a tokenized cost estimate and breakdown.
02:10 Rachel: From security - any data leaving our VPC is problematic. We need to see KMS integration and audit logs during the POC. If you can provide those logs as part of the artifact that's a must.
02:35 Priya: We support private deployment with KMS and audit trails. For the benchmark we'll record the access logs and share an anonymized log export.
03:02 Jordan: Great. Priya, can you walk the proposed benchmark workload and the acceptance criteria?
03:15 Priya: Sure. Plan is a 48-hour hammer run with steady-state and burst phases. Workload sizing: steady-state 40 RPS, concurrency 20, peak bursts up to 120 RPS for 10 minutes every 6 hours. Token profile: 70% short (<256), 20% medium (256-1024), 10% long (>1024).
03:47 Marcus: That profile looks similar to our real traffic, tho our peak bursts were closer to 180 RPS during campaign windows. we can expose that too if you want.
04:05 Priya: We can add a high-peak pass if you provide the expected peaks. For acceptance we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, error rate, and a quality signal from your eval set.
04:27 Ana: For quality we have an anonymization score and a semantic correctness metric. pass if anonymization failure rate <0.5% and semantic accuracy >= 92% on the eval set.
04:50 Jordan: So provisional acceptance thresholds: p95 latency <600ms for short prompts, error rate <0.5%, anonymization failure <0.5%, semantic accuracy >=92%, cost per 1M tokens under agreed threshold (TBD). Anything else?
05:12 Rachel: And security: successful KMS integration, logs available, and no data exfiltration observed. Also IP allowlist and RBAC verification.
05:28 Priya: We'll include a security checklist artifact: KMS key ARN(s) redacted in shared docs, sample audit log, and steps for RBAC validation.
05:44 Jordan: On reporting format — our suggested deliverables are: 1) A summary PDF with pass/fail flags, 2) Raw CSV exports with per-request timestamps, latencies, tokens in/out, error reason codes, 3) A Grafana dashboard snapshot with p95/p99 panels, and 4) A quality evaluation notebook (notebook and CSV).
06:22 Ana: CSV column names matter. can you include a header spec? our data team will plug it into our QA tools.
06:35 Priya: Yes header spec: timestamp_iso, request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, latency_ms, model_name, response_status, error_code (nullable), eval_score, anonymization_flag (0/1). We'll send a sample CSV.
07:02 Jordan: Good. on the go/no-go rubric we recommend a three-band outcome: Pass, Conditional Pass, Fail. Conditional Pass triggers remediation steps and a short remediation run. Does that align with your procurement needs?
07:22 Marcus: Yes, procurement needs a remediation window and defined rollback criteria. we also need a checklist of what constitutes a conditional pass vs fail.
07:38 Priya: Suggested mapping: Pass = all thresholds met. Conditional Pass = one non-security threshold missed by <=10% (e.g., p95=650ms when target 600ms) or cost slightly above target; requires a 72-hour remediation run. Fail = security threshold missed or multiple core thresholds failed.
08:05 Rachel: Security misses can't be remediated in place during the POC; they'd be immediate blockers. encryption keys and audit trails must be in place.
08:22 Ana: For the quality eval, if semantic accuracy falls between 88-92% we treat that as conditional with manual review of 200 samples. below 88 is fail.
08:40 Jordan: I'll add those numeric windows into the rubric doc. We'll keep the acceptance artifact machine-readable, so procurement and platform team can parse flags programmatically.
09:02 Marcus: On timelines, if we sign off today, we want the 48h benchmark run to start no later than 2026-06-16 and results in three business days after completion. Is that feasible?
09:18 Priya: Yes if you can provide the sample dataset and peak traffic numbers by 2026-06-16. we'll provision and run starting the same day or the next. the run itself is 48h plus 1 day analysis.
09:42 Ana: One nuance — some endpoints in our app stream tokens and use streaming. do you capture streaming latencies differently?
09:56 Priya: Streaming is measured as time-to-first-token and tokens-per-second during stream. We will include that as separate buckets in the CSV (ttft_ms, stream_tps).
10:18 Jordan: Good. On cost thresholds we left it TBD; we will surface an estimated token pricing based on model variants used in the run. Ana, do you have preferred models or is it flexible?
10:32 Ana: We'd like to test the smallest viable model that meets accuracy — if Redwood recommends a 13B quantized variant that meets the thresholds, that's preferred. we want the cost to be within our budget targets.
10:50 Priya: We'll run two variants: 13B quantized baseline and 33B float-ish baseline for quality checks. both will be in the run and included in the report.
11:10 Marcus: Regarding environment: we will prefer private deployment in our VPC. Redwood, will you need elevated firewall rules to allow benchmark agents?
11:26 Priya: We'll provide a small ingress list and an ephemeral SSH bastion config for the private-run agent. we'll share the runbook and infra checklist.
11:46 Rachel: And for logs we need assurances that the raw content isn't persisted in Redwood's hosted logs if private. Do you have a redact/no-persist option?
12:05 Priya: In Private mode all data stays in your environment; Redwood's control plane receives only operational metadata. We'll document exactly which artifacts leave the VPC and provide a sample anonymized log.
12:30 Jordan: Ok, next let's talk about the reporting template. Priya, could you show the example row and sample visual?
12:42 Priya: Example row (CSV): 2026-06-17T01:23:45Z, req-000123, 18, 56, 74, 412, redwood-13b-q, 200, , 0.94, 0
13:05 Ana: For the eval score 0.94 is that semantic accuracy? we want decimal representation, good.
13:17 Priya: Yes, eval_score is 0-1. anonymization_flag 1 means fail. We'll also attach a QA notebook that samples failing rows and gives human-readable examples.
13:40 Jordan: On the dashboard snapshot we'll include time-series for latency percentiles, error rate, throughput, and cost burn rate. For pass/fail we will calculate flags at the end and include a JSON artifact with boolean flags for each threshold.
14:02 Marcus: That JSON artifact is great because our automation can ingest it. please include schema.
14:14 Priya: Schema (brief): {"p95_short_ms": number, "error_rate_pct": number, "anonym_fail_pct": number, "semantic_acc": number, "cost_per_1m_tokens_usd": number, "security_ok": boolean}. We'll attach full JSON schema in the rubric doc.
14:42 Rachel: A small transcription glitch: we call out vendor egress costs as a concern. if you use hosted mode for the run be transparent about egress and storage costs.
15:01 Jordan: We'll include a cost appendix that lists expected compute, storage, and egress for both hosted and private runs.
15:18 Ana: Quick question — who signs off internally at Stratus? I'll need to loop procurement and our ML lead.
15:30 Marcus: Procurement will want the pass/fail matrix and remediation SLA. Legal will want the data flow diagram.
15:45 Rachel: Security needs time to review the audit log sample and KMS integration; give us the sample doc and a 48h window to review.
16:02 Jordan: Action items captured, thanks. Any other technical clarifications on telemetry?
16:12 Priya: One more: we'll enable token-level KV cache metrics if applicable; that helps explain cold/warm token behavior. We'll surface cache hit/miss rates.
16:32 Ana: That will help. Also can we get per-route breakdowns? our app has three routes with different SLAs.
16:45 Priya: Yes, we'll tag requests by route_id and provide per-route aggregates in the CSV and dashboard.
17:02 Marcus: About acceptance timing: if remediation is required what's a realistic remediation run length? you suggested 72 hours, is that fixed?
17:18 Priya: 72 hours is typical for single-issue tuning. If it's a model quality issue we may need an additional evaluation cycle — we'll define remediation scope in the rubric per issue.
17:36 Ana: For conditional pass, will you provide root-cause notes and proposed mitigation steps?
17:46 Jordan: Yes, remediation packet will include summary, root cause hypotheses, config changes we made, and a short rerun plan.
18:00 Rachel: From compliance, we also need to ensure logs are retained only for the agreed retention window and that deletion processes are documented.
18:12 Priya: We'll document retention and deletion steps, and provide a notarized deletion run summary after the POC if required.
18:30 Jordan: Ok last segment: signoff. We're looking for agreement on thresholds and deliverables so we can proceed to scheduling. I'll read back the key points: 1) 48h benchmark with the workload profile Priya described, 2) pass thresholds: p95_short_ms <600, error_rate <0.5%, anonymization_fail <0.5%, semantic_acc >=92%, security checks must pass, 3) deliverables: summary PDF, raw CSV (with header spec), Grafana snapshot, JSON pass/fail artifact, quality notebook, security checklist.
19:05 Ana: That matches our expectations. we also add conditional pass windows: <=10% tolerance on non-security thresholds, manual sample review for borderline quality.
19:22 Marcus: We'll provide sample dataset and peak numbers by 2026-06-16.
19:35 Rachel: Security will review artifacts within 48h after we receive them.
19:48 Jordan: Great — last thing, pricing: we'll send a draft estimate for compute and token costs as an appendix; that doesn't gate the POC acceptance but helps procurement.
20:02 Ana: Sounds good. Any blockers?
20:08 Priya: No blockers from our side. We'll create the rubic doc and artifact schema and share.
20:18 Jordan: Perfect. We'll target the benchmark for the week of 2026-06-16 as discussed. Thanks everyone.

(end of recorded transcript)
